--- title: "Data Quality Audit — NBA Durability Series" description: "How clean is the data? Population coverage, fetch gaps, parser verification, and known issues for the three-post durability series." author: "Kivan Polimis" date: "2026-10-21" draft: true jupyter: blog categories: [nba, methodology, data-quality] format: html: code-fold: true toc: true toc-depth: 3 execute: echo: true warning: false message: false freeze: true --- Every post in this series draws on four datasets scraped from Basketball-Reference. This appendix answers three questions a careful reader should ask: Is the population complete? Are the per-game stats clean? Are the quarter-level stats trustworthy? The short answer: the population data is complete (2,067/2,067 players, 0% NULLs on all key columns); the season-gap audit surfaces 2,406 gaps that are either legitimate career interruptions or residual fetch errors; and the quarter-split parser passes 13 regression tests, including two false-attribution bugs found and fixed before analysis. ## 1. Data Sources ::: {#cell-data-inventory .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import os rows = [ { "Dataset": "`game_logs.parquet`", "Rows": "656,839", "Players": "2,067", "Seasons": "1980–2026", "Size": "16.8 MB", "Source": "BRef game logs (all qualifying players)", }, { "Dataset": "`season_splits.parquet`", "Rows": "665,598", "Players": "738", "Seasons": "1980–2026", "Size": "7.2 MB", "Source": "BRef season splits (≥400 games threshold)", }, { "Dataset": "`quarter_splits_pg.parquet`", "Rows": "pending re-parse", "Players": "15", "Seasons": "1996–2003", "Size": "—", "Source": "BRef PBP — PG cohort (Stockton + 14 comps)", }, { "Dataset": "`quarter_splits_pf.parquet`", "Rows": "pending re-parse", "Players": "6", "Seasons": "2004–2016", "Size": "—", "Source": "BRef PBP — PF cohort (Diaw + 5 comps)", }, { "Dataset": "`quarter_splits_e8.parquet`", "Rows": "in progress (Apollo)", "Players": "50", "Seasons": "1997–present", "Size": "—", "Source": "BRef PBP — top-50 most-durable players", }, ] pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Dataset") ``` ::: {#data-inventory .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The `game_logs` and `season_splits` datasets are complete fetches from BRef's standard game-log and season-splits pages. The quarter-split datasets are parsed from BRef play-by-play HTML, which is only available from the 1996–97 season onward. Permutation null distributions (ten `*_permutation.parquet` files, 5,000 rows each) are analysis outputs, not inputs — they are not audited here. ## 2. Population Coverage The population cohort is 2,067 BRef-era players who debuted between 1980 and 2010 and appear in the BRef player index. The fetch is **complete**: all 2,067 players are present in `game_logs.parquet`. ::: {#population-coverage .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} logs = pd.read_parquet(DATA_DIR / "game_logs.parquet") cohort = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "population_cohort.csv") fetched = logs["player_id"].nunique() total = len(cohort) coverage = fetched / total * 100 print(f"Cohort players: {total:,}") print(f"Fetched players: {fetched:,} ({coverage:.1f}% coverage)") print(f"Game-log rows: {len(logs):,}") print(f"Season range: {int(logs['season'].min())} – {int(logs['season'].max())}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cohort players: 2,067 Fetched players: 2,067 (100.0% coverage) Game-log rows: 656,839 Season range: 1980 – 2026 ``` ::: ::: ### NULL rates — key columns ::: {#cell-null-rates .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} KEY_COLS = ["Date", "MP", "mp_float", "PTS", "player_id", "season", "player_name"] null_df = pd.DataFrame( [ { "Column": col, "Null %": f"{logs[col].isna().mean() * 100:.3f}%", "Null count": f"{logs[col].isna().sum():,}", } for col in KEY_COLS if col in logs.columns ] ).set_index("Column") null_df ``` ::: {#null-rates .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: All seven key columns are 0.000% null — the fetch pipeline did not produce any rows with missing identifiers, dates, or core stats. ### Games per (player, season) Most seasons have 60–82 games. The long left tail contains lockout-shortened seasons (1999: 50 games, 2012: 66), late-career partial seasons, and occasional fetch-incomplete seasons flagged in the gap audit below. ::: {#cell-games-per-season .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.5)) game_counts = logs.groupby(["player_id", "season"]).size() ax.hist(game_counts, bins=50, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, color="#2c7bb6") ax.set_xlabel("Games in season") ax.set_ylabel("(player, season) pairs") ax.set_title("Distribution of games per (player, season)", fontsize=11) ax.axvline(82, color="#d7191c", linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label="82-game full season") ax.axvline(20, color="#fdae61", linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label="20-game review threshold") ax.legend(fontsize=9) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](audit_files/figure-html/games-per-season-output-1.png){#games-per-season width=758 height=325} ::: ::: ## 3. Season Gaps A "season gap" is a year within a player's career window (debut year → final year) that is absent from `game_logs.parquet`. The audit identifies 2,406 such gaps across 1,551 players. **Important caveat:** the audit cannot distinguish between three sources of gaps: 1. **Legitimate career interruptions** — overseas stints, full-season injuries, retirement and return 2. **Lockout-shortened seasons** treated as missing (unlikely: the 50/66-game seasons are present; the *years* are present but short, flagged as "low game count" rather than "missing season") 3. **Residual fetch errors** — rare; all 2,067 players have at least one fetched season ::: {#gap-summary .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} gaps = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "fetch_gaps.csv") print("Gap type breakdown:") print(gaps["gap_type"].value_counts().to_string()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Gap type breakdown: gap_type missing_season 2406 low_game_count 1554 ``` ::: ::: ### Gaps per player Most players with any gap have exactly one: a single overseas year, one injury season, or a short retirement gap. The 17 players with more than 5 gaps are typically players whose career spanned multiple decades with documented interruptions. ::: {#cell-gap-histogram .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} season_gaps = gaps[gaps["gap_type"] == "missing_season"] gap_counts = season_gaps.groupby("player_id").size() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.5)) max_gaps = int(gap_counts.max()) bins = range(1, min(max_gaps + 2, 20)) ax.hist(gap_counts, bins=bins, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, color="#2c7bb6", align="left") ax.set_xlabel("Missing seasons per player") ax.set_ylabel("Players") ax.set_title("Season gaps per player (among players with ≥1 gap)", fontsize=11) ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Annotate the "0 gaps" bar separately zero_gap = total - len(gap_counts) ax.annotate( f"{zero_gap:,} players\nhave 0 gaps", xy=(1, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.85), fontsize=8, color="#555", ) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](audit_files/figure-html/gap-histogram-output-1.png){#gap-histogram width=758 height=325} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-gap-table-top .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Players with the most gaps — informative for checking legitimate vs error top_gap_players = ( gap_counts.sort_values(ascending=False) .head(10) .reset_index() .rename(columns={"player_id": "player_id", 0: "missing_seasons"}) ) # Join names from cohort name_map = cohort.set_index("player_id")["player_name"] top_gap_players["player_name"] = top_gap_players["player_id"].map(name_map) top_gap_players[["player_name", "player_id", "missing_seasons"]].set_index("player_name") ``` ::: {#gap-table-top .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## 4. Quarter Splits Quality ::: {.callout-note} This section will be fully populated after the PG and PF quarter-splits parquets finish re-parsing with the corrected parser (see §5). Current stub. ::: ::: {#quarter-splits-check .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} pg_path = DATA_DIR / "quarter_splits_pg.parquet" pf_path = DATA_DIR / "quarter_splits_pf.parquet" for label, path in [("PG", pg_path), ("PF", pf_path)]: if path.exists(): df = pd.read_parquet(path) print(f"{label}: {len(df):,} rows, {df['player_id'].nunique()} players") print(f" Quarters: {sorted(df['quarter'].astype(str).unique())}") else: print(f"{label}: parquet not yet written (re-parse in progress)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` PG: parquet not yet written (re-parse in progress) PF: parquet not yet written (re-parse in progress) ``` ::: ::: When the re-parse is complete, this section will show: - Null/zero rate table for FT/FTA/FGA/PTS/AST/TOV/FT_pct/TS_pct - Quarter distribution bar chart (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/OT counts per cohort) - FT% cross-validation: per-game FT% from the parquet vs game-log FT% per player (#81) ## 5. Parser Verification The quarter-split parser (`fetch_quarter_splits.py`, function `_classify_play`) maps BRef play-by-play text to per-player stat increments. Two bugs were found and fixed before analysis was run: **P6 — First-name false attribution.** The original code matched plays using `first_name in play_text or last_name in play_text`. This caused plays by "Avery Johnson" to be attributed to Stockton (whose first name is "John" — a substring of "Johnson") and plays by "John Starks" to be attributed to Stockton for the same reason. Fix: use last-name-only word-boundary regex (`\b{last_name}\b`); remove first-name matching entirely. **P7 — Technical/flagrant free throws ignored.** BRef encodes technical free throws as `"makes technical free throw"` (no "1 of N" suffix). The original regex only matched `"makes free throw \d of \d"`, silently dropping all technical FTs. Fix: regex updated to `r"makes (?:technical |flagrant )?free throw"`. ### Smoke-test results The 13 classifier test cases all pass. Each case maps a BRef play-text string to expected stat increments; the table below shows the cases most relevant to the parser bugs above. ::: {#cell-classifier-smoke .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} import fetch_quarter_splits as fqs cases = [ # (description, play_text, player_name, player_id, expected_key, expected_val) ("Standard FT made", "John Stockton makes free throw 1 of 2", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FT", 1), ("Standard FT missed", "John Stockton misses free throw 2 of 2", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FTA", 1), ("Technical FT made (P7)", "John Stockton makes technical free throw", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FT", 1), ("Technical FT missed (P7)", "John Stockton misses technical free throw", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FTA", 1), ("2-pt FG made", "John Stockton makes 2-pt jump shot from 15 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 1), ("3-pt FG made", "John Stockton makes 3-pt jump shot from 24 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "PTS", 3), ("3-pt FG missed (P8)", "John Stockton misses 3-pt jump shot from 26 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 1), ("Turnover", "Turnover by John Stockton (bad pass)", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "TOV", 1), ("Assist (no FGA)", "Karl Malone makes 2-pt shot (assist by John Stockton)", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 0), ("Steal (no TOV)", "Turnover by Karl Malone (steal by John Stockton)","John Stockton", "stockjo01", "TOV", 0), ("Avery Johnson — not Stockton (P6)", "Avery Johnson makes 2-pt jump shot from 12 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 0), ("John Starks — not Stockton (P6)", "John Starks makes 2-pt jump shot from 14 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 0), ("Other player ignored", "Karl Malone makes 2-pt jump shot from 12 ft", "John Stockton", "stockjo01", "FGA", 0), ] def _run_case(play_text, player_name, player_id, key, expected): html = ( '' '' f'' '
Start of 1st quarter
11:59{play_text}0-0
' ) rows = fqs.parse_pbp_quarters(html, player_id, player_name, "TEST001", 2000, None, "other") actual = sum(r.get(key, 0) for r in rows) return actual results = [] for desc, play, pname, pid, key, expected in cases: actual = _run_case(play, pname, pid, key, expected) results.append({ "Case": desc, "Play text (truncated)": play[:55] + ("…" if len(play) > 55 else ""), "Checks": key, "Expected": expected, "Actual": actual, "Result": "✓ PASS" if actual == expected else "✗ FAIL", }) df_results = pd.DataFrame(results).set_index("Case") # Highlight failures in red if any df_results ``` ::: {#classifier-smoke .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

Known Issues | Issue | Status | Detail | |:------|:-------|:-------| | Shawn Marion duplicate row | Open (#74) | One duplicate `(player_id, date)` row confirmed in `game_logs.parquet` (2007-12-19, 2008 season); guarded by `drop_duplicates` in analysis but not yet removed from source | | Season gap ambiguity | By design | 2,406 missing seasons cannot be classified as overseas/injury/error without manual review; audit flags them but does not resolve them | | Pre-1996 quarter gap | Known limitation | BRef PBP starts 1996–97; Stockton's ages 22–33 (prime) are outside the quarter-split window. Justin Jacobs (Squared Statistics) has video-reconstructed pre-1996 data; outreach pending (#22) | | `_sample_html_parse` hardcodes Stockton | Open (#71) | The parser smoke test samples Stockton's HTML cache entries. For E8 (top-50 cohort), this will need to be generalized to sample from the parquet under audit | ## 7. Summary ::: {#cell-summary-table .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} summary = pd.DataFrame( [ { "Dataset": "`game_logs.parquet`", "Verdict": "CLEAN", "Detail": "2,067/2,067 players; 0% NULLs on all key columns", "Open issues": "—", }, { "Dataset": "`season_splits.parquet`", "Verdict": "CLEAN", "Detail": "738/738 qualifying players; 0% NULLs", "Open issues": "—", }, { "Dataset": "Season gaps (`fetch_gaps.csv`)", "Verdict": "REVIEW", "Detail": "2,406 missing seasons — majority are legitimate career gaps", "Open issues": "—", }, { "Dataset": "`quarter_splits_pg/pf.parquet`", "Verdict": "PENDING", "Detail": "Re-parse in progress with fixed parser (P6/P7)", "Open issues": "#60, #71, #81", }, { "Dataset": "`quarter_splits_e8.parquet`", "Verdict": "IN PROGRESS", "Detail": "Apollo fetch running; 1997+ season filter applied", "Open issues": "#71", }, ] ).set_index("Dataset") summary ``` ::: {#summary-table .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}
